transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me?

Hi, thanks. Um, well, I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant, and I just keep starting my tasks—like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork—and I somehow always leave out the last parts. 

It's becoming a huge problem because I know my job completely depends on finishing those forms and steps correctly, but I just... don't follow through to the end of them.
Has this tendency to leave tasks unfinished been something you've noticed since you were a child, or is this a new pattern that started more recently?

It's definitely not a new thing. It's been happening since I was a kid. 

My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade, and they say pretty much the same thing. The teachers would write that I was bright, but that I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn my homework in. I remember I would understand the lessons perfectly fine, but I would just... miss whole chunks of the instructions unless the teacher stayed right close to me to keep me on track.

Growing up and even now, have you also struggled with things like feeling restless, needing to move around a lot, fidgeting, talking excessively, or acting impulsively without thinking things through?

No, not really. I've never been the type to bounce off the walls or anything like that. I don't really fidget much or talk a lot, and I don't think I act impulsively. It's really just the focusing and finishing things that I struggle with, not the physical energy part.
Do you notice this same pattern of losing focus and not finishing things in other areas of your life too, like at home, when managing personal finances, or in social situations—not just at work?

Um, I'm not really sure about that. I haven't really noticed it as much at home or with my money... or in social situations, really. 

I mean, maybe I do, but I just haven't paid attention to it. It's really just at the plant where it's causing such a massive issue right now, so that's mostly what I know. I don't really have any specific examples for those other areas.
Can you think of a specific example at home—like paying a bill, doing laundry, or finishing a chore—where you started something but didn't complete the final steps?

Um, honestly... no, I really can't think of one. Like I said, I just haven't noticed it happening outside of work. 

I mean, when I get home from the plant, I'm usually pretty tired, so I mostly just relax. I don't really have a lot of big chores or complicated bills to manage right now anyway. So... yeah, I can't really picture a time where I started laundry or something and just didn't finish the steps. It's really just at work where it's a huge problem for me.

Outside of work, when you're doing something you enjoy or care about—like a hobby, a personal project, or even reading a book—do you ever notice yourself starting it but not following through to the end?

Honestly, no. If it's something I actually care about or enjoy doing, I don't really have an issue finishing it. 

I don't have a ton of hobbies right now anyway. Mostly I just watch TV or hang out after my shift at the plant. But yeah, if I start a movie or a game or something that I actually like, I'll finish it. Like I was saying, I really only notice this being a problem when I'm at work.
Going back to when you were a kid, did your parents ever mention you having similar trouble finishing chores or tasks at home, even if it wasn't as noticeable as the school issues?

Well, my mom actually still has my old elementary school report cards, like from around fourth grade. And they pretty much all said the same thing—that I was bright, but I needed constant reminders to actually finish my classwork and turn in my homework. 

I remember I would understand the lessons fine, but I would just miss chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was standing right there next to me to keep me on track. So yeah, I guess it was definitely an issue back then too.

Have you noticed a similar pattern with other paperwork-type tasks outside of work—like filling out medical forms, tax documents, or applications—where you start them but don't complete the final steps?

Um, not really, no. I mean, I guess I don't really have a lot of paperwork like that to deal with right now anyway. But when I do have to fill something out, like at the doctor's office or whatever, I usually just get it done right then and there. So no, I haven't really noticed that being a problem for me outside of the plant.
Before working at this plant, did you have any other jobs, and if so, did you notice this same kind of trouble finishing tasks or paperwork there as well?

No, this is actually my first real full-time job since I graduated. I had some part-time stuff during college, like working the register at a grocery store, but that didn't really involve paperwork or long tasks. You just ring people up and bag their stuff. So, yeah, I didn't really have to deal with anything like this until I started at the plant.
Thinking back to college, did you ever have trouble completing all the steps of an assignment or project—like finishing every required section of a paper or lab report—before turning it in?

Um, I don't really remember that being a big issue. I mean, I struggled with getting things done on time, for sure, but if I actually got the paper or the lab report done, I usually did all the parts of it. I don't think I made a habit of leaving sections blank or anything like that before turning it in.
Do you often forget everyday things—like appointments, where you put your keys or phone, or tasks someone asked you to do—outside of work?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I always know where my phone is, and my keys are usually just in my purse or on the counter. I don't really miss appointments either, mostly because I just put them in my calendar right away. So, no, forgetting everyday stuff like that hasn't really been a problem for me.

Would you say the sanitation steps, batch logs, and paperwork you don't finish are tasks you find boring or tedious compared to other parts of your job, or does it happen even with tasks you don't mind doing?

Um, I'm not really sure if it's just about them being boring. I mean, the batch logs and sanitation steps aren't exactly fun, but I don't really know if I leave them unfinished just because they're tedious. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. It just seems like I run out of time or get sidetracked, no matter what I'm doing.

Do you tend to avoid or put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort or careful organization—like planning a trip, organizing your finances, or filling out complex forms—even outside of work?

Not really, no. I mean, if I have to fill out a form for something or deal with my bank account, I just kind of get it over with. I don't think I avoid them or put them off just because they take a lot of thinking or planning. I haven't really noticed that being an issue for me.
Has anything changed recently at the plant—like increased workload, understaffing, or tighter deadlines—that might explain why finishing these tasks has become such a problem now?

No, not really. Everything at the plant is pretty much the same as it's always been. The workload hasn't changed, and we have the same amount of people on the floor. The deadlines are the same, too. So, no, I can't really blame it on anything like that. It's just... me, I guess.

Aside from the trouble finishing tasks, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, energy, or interest in things—like feeling down, unmotivated, or less interested in activities you used to enjoy?

No, I don't think so. My mood has been fine, and I still like doing the things I usually do. I'm not feeling down or anything like that. My energy is pretty normal, too. It's really just the issue with finishing my work tasks that's been bothering me.
Do you ever notice your mind wandering or losing track of what someone is saying while they're talking directly to you, even in casual conversations outside of work?

Yes, that definitely happens. It's actually a big problem when my supervisor gives me directions face-to-face. I’ll stand there and nod like I’m following along with everything she's saying, but... a minute later, I realize I only remember the first piece of what she said. I usually have to go ask someone else what she just told me to do.
